text: [{"id":8,"latex":"Another reason philosophers have given for the existence of the is-ought gap is that it is just a special case of a general principle of logic: one cannot validly deduce a conclusion that applies a predicate $P$, from premises that nowhere contain that predicate.¹⁷ This is nothing special about evaluative predicates; it applies to any predicate whatsoever. For instance, one cannot infer a conclusion stating that something is red from premises that nowhere contain the word 'red'."}]
